draft.title: Angles of any size
card: For an angle beyond 90°, find its related acute angle: the acute angle it makes with the x-axis. The trig ratio has the same size as the ratio of that acute angle.
The quadrant gives the sign. In quadrant 1 all ratios are positive. In quadrant 2 only sin is positive. In quadrant 3 only tan is positive. In quadrant 4 only cos is positive.
Related acute angle: in quadrant 2 it is 180° − θ. In quadrant 3 it is θ − 180°. In quadrant 4 it is 360° − θ. In radians, use π in place of 180° and 2π in place of 360°.
Example: sin 150°. It is in quadrant 2, so the related angle is 180° − 150° = 30° and sin is positive. So sin 150° = sin 30° = 1/2.
draft.remember: Find the related acute angle for the size, then use the quadrant for the sign.

a.q: What is the value of cos 120°?
a.why: 120° is in quadrant 2, so the related angle is 180° − 120° = 60°. Cos is negative in quadrant 2, so cos 120° = −cos 60° = −1/2. The option 1/2 has the right size but ignores the sign.
a.clue: Find the related angle, then check the sign in quadrant 2.

b.q: What is the value of tan (5π/4)?
b.why: 5π/4 is between π and 3π/2, so it is in quadrant 3. The related angle is 5π/4 − π = π/4, and tan (π/4) = 1. Tan is positive in quadrant 3, so the answer is 1. The option −1 comes from wrongly treating tan as negative here.
b.clue: Subtract π to get the related angle, then check the sign in quadrant 3.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's related-angle and quadrant-sign rules are correct, and the intended answers (cos 120° = −1/2, tan 5π/4 = 1) and their explanations are right.
